learning_outcomes.text: Know and apply material selection criteria.
Know and apply non-destructive tests used in material control.
Perform tests in the materials laboratory, collect, analyze, and interpret the resulting data and draw conclusions.
Able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Design and selection for mechanical properties
Topic 2. Introduction to quality control systems
Definitions of quality, quality control, and standardization
Development of Quality Control and Reliability systems
Justification for the use of non-destructive testing
Fields of application for non-destructive testing
Topic 4: Analysis of new methods and emerging techniques of special application in the industrial field
assessment_rules: The final grade is a weighted average of the laboratory grade (65%) and the exam grade (35%). The student passes the course when their final grade is equal to or greater than 5. The laboratory grade is kept if it is 5 or higher; otherwise, the student must retake the laboratory part in the final exam. Exam grades are not kept, so students failing continuous assessment will be re-evaluated on all course material in the ordinary and/or extraordinary resit exams.
